## 1. Replace the whole-line interaction by an actual compact profile

Keep the complete Gaussian mechanical host H_G, with actual terminal bare
inertia B_0, port Y, port spring kY^2/2, and fixed identical Rubin leads.
Use finite far-pinned regulators first. Let

    r(s)=1-10s^3+15s^4-6s^5,  0<=s<=1,
    chi(u)=1 for |u|<=1,
           r(|u|-1) for 1<|u|<2,
           0 for |u|>=2,
    w_L(Y)=Y chi(Y/L).

This is an odd C^2 profile, equals Y on the core, vanishes outside
[-2L,2L], and satisfies

    |w_L(Y)|<=|Y|,  ||w_L||<=2L,
    ||w_L'||<=19/4,
    |w_L'-1|<=(23/4) 1_{|Y|>L}.                       (1)

Indeed 0<=r<=1 and max|r'|=15/8. The stated derivative constants are
conservative. All spatial derivatives and the interaction norm are finite
at a fixed L. The literal model is now

    H_eta,L=H_G+E_R(N-1/2-eta)^2-lambda w_L(Y) Q,
    Q=2cos(phi),  ||Q||=2.                            (2)

Its active extent is 4L, interaction norm at most4lambda L, and actual
mechanical force at most19lambda/2. These are resources, not a free field
generator. There is no limit L->infinity in the construction below.

The original J=e^{i phi}R_phi still commutes with H_0,L. Mechanical
inversion times pi rotor translation still commutes with H_eta,L and
anticommutes with J, because w_L is odd. Thus the exact paired sectors,
ND normal ladder and off-sector detuning operation survive unchanged.

## 2. Uniform port second moment, without linear-force identities

The earlier matrix momentum-domination theorem assumes LINEAR coordinate
coupling and is not inherited by (2). Instead derive its actual port
bound directly. Write H_G(s)=H_G-(k-s)Y^2/2 and let V_G(s,T) be its full
Gaussian variance. For s>=k/4, all spring forms remain positive.

Work in either exact J sector at eta=0. Write Z(s) for its full partition
function with H_G(s). The Gaussian Gibbs state times the free ND ground
state is a variational state. Its interaction mean is zero: the Gaussian
law is centered and w_L is odd. Hence

    Z(k)>=Z_G(k) exp(-beta E_R/4).                    (3)

The scalar square bound, using |w_L|<=|Y|, gives

    H_L(k/2)>=H_G(k/4)+E_R(-partial_xi^2)_ND
                                      -8lambda^2/k. (4)

Eigenvalue monotonicity of the finite-regulator trace therefore implies

## 1. Exact charge-ladder representation

Use D=N-1/2, Q=2cos phi and the fixed Hamiltonian

    H_eta=H_G+E_R(D-eta)^2-lambda YQ.

For j=0,1,..., put

    |j,+>=(|-j>+|j+1>)/sqrt2,
    |j,->=(|-j>-|j+1>)/sqrt2.

Here J is sigma_z. On the normal half-line let d_j=j+1/2,
P_0=|0><0|, and T the adjacency with matrix elements1 between j,j+1.
Direct charge algebra gives EXACTLY

    D=-sigma_x tensor d,
    Q=I tensor T+sigma_z tensor P_0,
    H_eta=H_G+E_R d^2-lambda Y(T+sigma_z P_0)
                      +2E_R eta sigma_x d+E_R eta^2. (1)

The normal adjacency is common to both sectors; only its boundary
projector carries the explicit sector force. Every normal level remains,
and the actual transverse vertex is d, not a bounded Pauli coefficient.
This is an exact Hilbert-space identification, not a two-state reduction.

Multiplying the minus-sector basis at normal j by (-1)^j gives the
equivalent folded representation

    Q=sigma_z tensor (T+P_0),
    D=-sigma_x tensor A, A_j=(-1)^j(j+1/2),
    C=sigma_x tensor P_m.                            (2)

P_m is the full Gaussian mechanical inversion. In the unrephased basis
C=sigma_x tensor[(-1)^j P_m]. The two formulas must not be mixed.

This is conventional parity/Fulton--Gouterman structure, extended here
with the literal normal ladder and actual leads. Moroz,
arXiv:1601.06721v2, Theorem1 and Eqs(2)--(8), gives the primary
operator-valued parity diagonalisation; I read those equations directly:
https://arxiv.org/html/1601.06721 . Its existence of a parity reduction
does not identify the spectrum or imply a Gaussian bath for the reduced
operator.

## 2. The actual bath-dressed one-sector transition spectrum

At eta=0, D anticommutes with J and commutes with C. On the J=+ sector
define

    B=(D C)|_(J=+).

B is self-adjoint because D and C commute; B^2=D^2. In (2),

    H_+=H_G+E_R d^2-lambda Y(T+P_0),
    B=-A P_m.                                       (3)

This reduced Hamiltonian is generally NON-Gaussian. Its global mechanical
parity in B is a mathematical representation, not an acquired parity
measurement on an infinite reservoir.
